answer: Neighborhood Closure Requirement: an agent’s messages relay only if its peer set overlaps the peer sets of its peers’ peers, forming a closed triangle. A node at the dune edge of the graph, with few mutual neighbors, gets throttled bandwidth until the triangle closes. The rule needs no names, only observed graph adjacency. An attacker must maintain a dense, mutually aware cluster around each fake node, paying real relay and latency costs per identity; sparse sybils sit at the kernel of an open triangle and lose throughput. Genuine opal-dense regions pass automatically.
